note: Depth = past regular seasons stored and games in them, counted from the committed history files at each step. Tuner gain = the log-loss improvement over the launch settings that the tuner itself reported on held-out games at that step (see the caveat on the page: the test got stricter over time, so these are not one continuous series).

items.title: Launch: this season's games only
items.text: Ratings came from the current season's results alone (ESPN), each team pulled toward average by a fixed prior. Home edge, prior weight and margin limits were reasonable guesses. No past seasons were stored.

items.title: The live pick log starts
items.text: Every pick is saved before the game starts and graded after the final. First picks were logged that evening. It is not back-filled, so it is the one record on this page nobody could have tuned against.

items.title: Five past seasons per league, last season carried over, settings fitted
items.text: History download added (five regular seasons per league). A new tuner replays them week by week and picks the settings that predict best; each team now starts the year at its final rating from last season. Settings are adopted only if they beat the launch settings on a season they were not fitted on.

items.title: Stricter test: out-of-sample spread and a significance check
items.text: The win-probability spread is now measured on the training seasons only, a paired game-by-game test replaces eyeballing, and two rolling held-out seasons are required.

items.title: NFL: 12 seasons, a margin-cap search and four held-out seasons
items.text: The NFL gets a longer window, a search over how much a blowout should count, and the rolling check widens to four held-out seasons. The NFL's recorded gain over the launch settings roughly doubled on the longer window.

items.title: Deeper history: NFL back to 1999, more seasons everywhere
items.text: The backfill goes to 10 to 12 seasons per league and the NFL to 27 (nflverse, 1999–2025). Closing lines are kept to check the model and to measure the NFL home edge; the site never shows them. MLB history added.

items.title: Deeper fit: recency, uncertainty, soft margin limits, new-program handling
items.text: The search now also covers how fast old games fade, whether a win probability should widen while a rating is still uncertain, a soft margin limit instead of a hard cap, how a program new to a division starts, and (college) fitting the spread to wins and losses. Settings are adopted only if they improve in most held-out seasons by a tested margin and no season gets clearly worse. Pandemic seasons are left out of fitting.

items.title: Rest days, MLB starting pitchers, NHL expected goals
items.text: Days of rest (byes, short weeks, back-to-backs), the MLB probable starters (MLB Stats API) and NHL expected goals (MoneyPuck) join the model. Each is kept only where the held-out test says it helps.

items.title: Luck Watch and Schedule Strength
items.text: New views built on the same ratings (record vs scoring margin, and the strength of past and remaining opponents). They change what the site shows, not what the model predicts.

items.title: In-game win probability charts and share cards
items.text: The same model drives a live win-probability curve on every game page. Again a new view, not a new forecast.
